title: All Palindromes Over k Letters

concept.title: Choose half of the word, the other half is forced
body: A palindrome of length `n` is decided by its **first half**: the letter at position `i` and the letter at position `n - 1 - i` must be equal. So the search only chooses the letters of positions `0 .. (n - 1) / 2`, and each choice is written to **both** positions. In the middle of an odd word the two positions are the same cell.

There is no undo step here: the next letter for the same positions simply **overwrites** the previous one, and the later positions are always written again before they are used. Whenever a choice can only be replaced by another choice, no explicit "unchoose" is needed. Because we try the letters in alphabetical order, the palindromes come out in dictionary order, and there are only `k^((n + 1) / 2)` of them.

statement: Print all palindromes of length `n` made of the first `k` lowercase letters (`a`, `b`, ...), in dictionary order, one per line.
outputFormat: The palindromes in dictionary order, one per line.

examples.note: The palindromes are aaa, aba, bab and bbb.

hints: Only the first half of the word is chosen freely.
When you choose the letter at position i, write it also at position n - 1 - i.
Try the letters in alphabetical order to get the dictionary order.

starter.python:
n, k = map(int, input().split())

# Your code here

explanation: The recursion fills positions `0 .. (n - 1) / 2` and mirrors each letter to position `n - 1 - pos`. When the first half is complete the word is a palindrome and is recorded; the alphabetical loop gives dictionary order.
solution.complexity: Time O(k^((n + 1) / 2) * n), space O(n) besides the output.

code.python:
def build(n, k, pos, word, out):
    if pos == (n + 1) // 2:
        out.append("".join(word))
        return
    for c in range(k):
        letter = chr(ord("a") + c)
        word[pos] = word[n - 1 - pos] = letter
        build(n, k, pos + 1, word, out)

n, k = map(int, input().split())

out = []
build(n, k, 0, ["a"] * n, out)
print("\n".join(out))
